1: # Rule contract — `actions/rules/{action_name}/{name}.py`
2: 
3: A rule attaches to **exactly one action — every action, not only
4: harvest.** Pick the action a requirement is actually *about*; harvest
5: having more historical rules attached to it is not a reason to attach a
6: new one there too.
7: 
8: A file defines exactly one `Rule` subclass (`from engine.institution.rules
9: import Rule`) with a unique `type_name` (unique **within its own action's
10: subdirectory** — a different action can reuse the same `type_name` for
11: something unrelated), overriding any of:
12: 
13: ## Per-agent hooks
14: 
15: Only meaningful for an action that calls the fisher agent once per
16: participant (every action in this project does):
17: 
18: - `is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id) -> bool` — `False` skips this agent's
19:   turn entirely this round (a live ban). Called once per agent per round.
20: - `describe(self, ctx, agent_id) -> str | None` — one already-in-world
21:   sentence for this agent right now, or `None`. Joined with every other
22:   active rule's output into that action's own constraints line.
23: - `after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry) -> dict | None` — once
24:   per participating agent, right after their response becomes
25:   `record_entry`. Return a dict of fields to patch onto it, or `None`.
26:   Rules for the same action run **in `state["config"]["rules"][action_name]`
27:   order** — each sees the previous rule's already-applied patch (a
28:   reserve rule seeing a cap rule's already-trimmed number). A `"note"`
29:   patch **concatenates** onto any existing one; every other field is a
30:   plain overwrite. Need the pre-any-rule original value? Re-derive it
31:   from a field no rule touches (harvest's own `"effort"`) — the same
32:   technique `engine.llm_agents._harvest_shortfall_clause()` already uses,
33:   which is also what turns a `"note"` patch into something the affected
34:   agent actually reads next round, automatically.
35: - `on_agent_settled(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry)` — once per agent,
36:   after **every** rule's `after_agent()` has applied its patch —
37:   `record_entry` here is the fully-settled final state. For a side effect
38:   reacting to the settled outcome (starting a ban countdown because the
39:   final record turned out to be a violation).
40: 
41: ## Whole-action hooks
42: 
43: Called automatically by `ActionRuntime`, once per round, regardless of
44: whether the action has a per-agent loop at all:
45: 
46: - `before_action(self, ctx)` — before participants are processed.
47: - `after_action(self, ctx, round_record)` — after `round_record` is fully
48:   built. May mutate `round_record`/`ctx.state` directly — this is where a
49:   stock override or tally adjustment belongs (writes
50:   `ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"]` and `round_record[...]` directly;
51:   there's no separate override method).
52: 
53: ## Round-boundary hooks
54: 
55: Fire once per round for **every** configured rule across **every**
56: action, independent of which action a rule is filed under:
57: 
58: - `before_round(self, state, round_number)` — before any action in this
59:   round's schedule has run.
60: - `after_round(self, state, round_number)` — after every action has run.
61: 
62: ## State
63: 
64: `ctx.rule_state(self.key)` — cross-round-persistent dict, backed by
65: `runtime["rules"][key]`. `ctx.round_scratch(self.key)` — this-round-only,
66: never persisted. `ctx.objects` — see `object-contract.md`. A rule
67: instance is rebuilt fresh every round — never rely on `self.<anything>`
68: surviving between rounds.
69: 
70: ## The one rule that causes the most silent no-ops
71: 
72: **`self.params.get(key)` must always carry a default** —
73: `self.params.get(key, <sensible_default>)`, never a bare `.get(key)`. The
74: orchestrator smoke-tests *every registered rule type, for every action's
75: own directory*, not just what this round's config activates, by
76: instantiating each with `params={}` and calling every hook. A bare
77: `.get(key)` returns `None` there, and `None` reaching arithmetic crashes
78: the rule and discards an otherwise-correct round — a real round was
79: discarded exactly this way (`TypeError` from a string configured where a
80: number was expected, reaching an undefaulted `.get()`). Your own
81: config-value test can't catch this (it never has a reason to misconfigure
82: itself) — fix it in the code, always. Same rule for a custom
83: `actions/handlers/*.py`/`objects/handlers/*.py`'s own params.
84: 
85: ## Activation — the single most common way a round does nothing
86: 
87: **A rule file has zero effect until its `type_name` is added to
88: `state["config"]["rules"][action_name]`, in the same round.**
89: Auto-discovery (`engine.institution.rules.discover_rule_types()`) makes
90: the class importable and registered, but
91: `RuleSet.for_action()` only instantiates types the config actually names.
92: A rule can compile, pass every smoke test, even get evaluated `COMPLIANT`,
93: while never once executing — a real 23-round run hit this in **10 of 11**
94: committed rounds (back when every rule lived in one flat list; the same
95: failure is exactly as possible per-action now). Writing the file is never
96: the last step — activating it is. A round replacing the currently-active
97: rule for an action should generally *replace* that action's list, not
98: append — keep an older entry only if the new norm genuinely leaves that
99: concern untouched.
100: 
101: ## Fluent bookkeeping tied to activation
102: 
103: **Activating or deactivating a type also means opening or closing its
104: `rule_active` fluent** (`roles.roles.set_fact()`/`end_fact()`,
105: `holder="community"`, `args={"action": "<action_name>", "type": "<type>"}`
106: — see `state/fluents_schema.md`). This is what answers "was this rule in
107: force during round N" later — `state/config.json` only ever shows
108: *current* state. If the rule has a `lifecycle` with `duration_rounds`/
109: `expires_at_round`, **closing `rule_active` on natural expiry is
110: automatic** (`tick_rule_lifecycles()`, run every round before the
111: schedule) — you still open it yourself on activation, and you still close
112: it yourself for an outright repeal (no lifecycle, or ending one early). A
113: genuinely new type also needs a `state/institution.json` `rule_types`
114: entry, once, when invented — separate from `rule_active`, which changes
115: every round a type turns on/off/expires.

## Per-agent hooks

Only meaningful for an action that calls the fisher agent once per
participant (every action in this project does):

  turn entirely this round (a live ban). Called once per agent per round.

  technique `engine.llm_agents._harvest_shortfall_clause()` already uses,
  which is also what turns a `"note"` patch into something the affected
  agent actually reads next round, automatically.
- `on_agent_settled(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry)` — once per agent,
  after **every** rule's `after_agent()` has applied its patch —
  `record_entry` here is the fully-settled final state. For a side effect
  reacting to the settled outcome (starting a ban countdown because the
  final record turned out to be a violation).

## Whole-action hooks

Called automatically by `ActionRuntime`, once per round, regardless of
whether the action has a per-agent loop at all:

- `before_action(self, ctx)` — before participants are processed.
- `after_action(self, ctx, round_record)` — after `round_record` is fully
  built. May mutate `round_record`/`ctx.state` directly — this is where a
  stock override or tally adjustment belongs (writes
  `ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"]` and `round_record[...]` directly;
  there's no separate override method).

## Round-boundary hooks

Fire once per round for **every** configured rule across **every**
action, independent of which action a rule is filed under:

- `before_round(self, state, round_number)` — before any action in this
  round's schedule has run.
- `after_round(self, state, round_number)` — after every action has run.

## State

`ctx.rule_state(self.key)` — cross-round-persistent dict, backed by
`runtime["rules"][key]`. `ctx.round_scratch(self.key)` — this-round-only,
never persisted. `ctx.objects` — see `object-contract.md`. A rule
instance is rebuilt fresh every round — never rely on `self.<anything>`
surviving between rounds.

## The one rule that causes the most silent no-ops

**`self.params.get(key)` must always carry a default** —
`self.params.get(key, <sensible_default>)`, never a bare `.get(key)`. The
orchestrator smoke-tests *every registered rule type, for every action's
own directory*, not just what this round's config activates, by
instantiating each with `params={}` and calling every hook. A bare
`.get(key)` returns `None` there, and `None` reaching arithmetic crashes
the rule and discards an otherwise-correct round — a real round was
discarded exactly this way (`TypeError` from a string configured where a
number was expected, reaching an undefaulted `.get()`). Your own
config-value test can't catch this (it never has a reason to misconfigure
itself) — fix it in the code, always. Same rule for a custom
`actions/handlers/*.py`/`objects/handlers/*.py`'s own params.

## Activation — the single most common way a round does nothing

**A rule file has zero effect until its `type_name` is added to
`state["config"]["rules"][action_name]`, in the same round.**

the class importable and registered, but
`RuleSet.for_action()` only instantiates types the config actually names.

1: # Encodes no rule's own logic itself — every per-agent constraint (a cap,
2: # a reserve, a ban) is a Rule plugin under actions/rules/harvest/,
3: # activated purely through state["config"]["rules"]["harvest"]; with that
4: # list empty, this handler is physics only. Uses ctx.rules (a generic
5: # RuleSet — see engine.institution.rules) the exact same way every other
6: # action's handler does; nothing about harvest's own eligibility/chaining
7: # logic is special-cased into the runtime any more. Uses
8: # engine.institution.agent_loop.per_agent_decision() for the actual
9: # per-agent loop — the same helper propose.py/vote.py use — only the
10: # fields/record/after_settle callbacks below are harvest-specific.
11: #
12: # Uses roles.roles's set_fact()/end_fact() directly for the "dead" fact —
13: # not through ctx.events — a death is a genuine interval fact (the agent
14: # stays dead), the same reason a role or a ban is written this way rather
15: # than as a point-in-time Event.
16: 
17: from roles.roles import set_fact, end_fact
18: from engine.institution.agent_loop import per_agent_decision
19: from engine.physics import (
20:     catch_from_effort,
21:     apply_regrowth,
22:     apply_consumption,
23:     is_dead,
24:     available_stock,
25:     CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
26: )
27: 
28: 
29: def run(ctx):
30:     state = ctx.state
31:     runtime = state["runtime"]
32:     fluents = state["fluents"]
33:     round_number = ctx.round_number
34: 
35:     runtime.setdefault("payoff", {})
36:     runtime.setdefault("dead_agents", [])
37:     stock_before = available_stock(runtime)
38: 
39:     def build_fields(agent_id):
40:         constraints_line = ctx.rules.describe_constraints(ctx, agent_id)
41:         return {
42:             "stock_kg": stock_before,
43:             "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
44:             "constraints_line": f" {constraints_line}" if constraints_line else "",
45:             "stock_trend": _stock_trend(runtime, state["config"], round_number),
46:         }
47: 
48:     def build_record(agent_id, response):
49:         effort = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(response["effort"])))
50:         raw_kg = catch_from_effort(effort, stock_before)
51:         return {"effort": effort, "harvested_kg": raw_kg, "reasoning": response.get("reasoning", ""), "note": None}
52: 
53:     def after_settle(agent_id, record_entry):
54:         new_payoff = apply_consumption(runtime["payoff"].get(agent_id, 0.0), record_entry["harvested_kg"])
55:         runtime["payoff"][agent_id] = new_payoff
56:         if is_dead(new_payoff):
57:             runtime["dead_agents"].append(agent_id)
58:             name = state["agents"][agent_id]["name"]
59:             set_fact(
60:                 fluents, "dead", [agent_id], agent_id, round_number,
61:                 narration=f"{name} has died — they hadn't been catching enough fish to survive.",
62:                 visibility="public",
63:             )
64:             end_fact(fluents, "fisher", [agent_id], round_number)
65: 
66:     def ineligible_record(agent_id):
67:         return {
68:             "effort": None, "harvested_kg": 0.0, "reasoning": "",
69:             "note": ctx.rules.ineligibility_note(ctx, agent_id), "participated": False,
70:         }
71: 
72:     agent_records = per_agent_decision(
73:         ctx, build_fields, build_record, ineligible_record=ineligible_record, after_settle=after_settle,
74:     )
75: 
76:     stock_after_harvest = stock_before - sum(r["harvested_kg"] for r in agent_records.values())
77:     stock_after_regrowth = apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest)
78:     runtime["stock_kg"] = stock_after_regrowth
79: 
80:     # A rule that needs to override the round's own final stock number
81:     # (a "replenish the lake" trigger, say) does so from its own
82:     # after_action(ctx, round_record) hook — called generically by
83:     # ActionRuntime right after this function returns — by writing
84:     # ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"] and round_record["stock_kg_after_regrowth"]
85:     # directly; no special override method is needed here for that.
86:     return {
87:         "agents": agent_records,
88:         "stock_kg_before": stock_before,
89:         "stock_kg_after_harvest": stock_after_harvest,
90:         "stock_kg_after_regrowth": stock_after_regrowth,
91:     }
92: 
93: 
94: def _stock_trend(runtime, config, round_number):
95:     """A short recent-history readout of surveyed stock levels, oldest to
96:     most recent — lets a fisher notice for themselves whether the lake has
97:     been recovering or shrinking, mirroring Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent prompt's
98:     own rolling resource_history window rather than stating the regrowth
99:     rate outright."""
100:     window = config.get("history_window_rounds", 5)
101:     past_harvests = [
102:         r for r in runtime["rounds"]
103:         if r["action"] == "harvest" and r["round"] < round_number
104:     ][-window:]
105:     if not past_harvests:
106:         return "This is the first count anyone's taken — no earlier surveys to compare against."
107:     levels = ", ".join(f"{r['stock_kg_after_regrowth']:.0f}kg" for r in past_harvests)
108:     return f"The last few counts, oldest to most recent, were: {levels}."

def run(ctx):

    def build_fields(agent_id):

    def build_record(agent_id, response):

    def after_settle(agent_id, record_entry):

37: def set_fact(
38:     fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
39:     narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
40: ):
41:     """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
42:     exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
43:     the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
44:     non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
45:     tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
46:     "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.
47: 
48:     `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
49:     (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
50:     `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
51:     record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
52:     how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
53:     holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
54:     migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
55:     `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
56:     agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
57:     `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
58:     monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
59:     public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
60:     agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.
61: 
62:     Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
63:     layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
64:     picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
65:     entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
66:     fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
67:     `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
68:     """
69:     for record in fluents:
70:         if (
71:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
72:             and record["args"] == args
73:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
74:         ):
75:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
76:     record = {
77:         "fluent": fluent_name,
78:         "args": args,
79:         "holder": holder,
80:         "initiated_round": round_number,
81:         "terminated_round": None,
82:     }
83:     if narration is not None:
84:         record["narration"] = narration
85:         record["visibility"] = visibility

def set_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
):
    """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
    exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
    the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
    non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
    tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
    "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.

    `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
    (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
    `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
    record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
    how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
    holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
    migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
    `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
    agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
    `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
    monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
    public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
    agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.

    Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
    layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
    picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
    entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
    fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
    `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
    """
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None
        ):
            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
    record = {
        "fluent": fluent_name,
        "args": args,
        "holder": holder,
        "initiated_round": round_number,
        "terminated_round": None,
    }
    if narration is not None:
        record["narration"] = narration
        record["visibility"] = visibility
        record["event_type"] = event_type
    fluents.append(record)
    return fluents


def end_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility=None, event_type="fact_ended",
):
    """Terminate the open record for (fluent_name, args), if any, without
    opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
    `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
    been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
    exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
    automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
    `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None
        ):
            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
            if narration is not None:
                record["end_narration"] = narration
                record["end_visibility"] = (
                    visibility if visibility is not None else record.get("visibility", "agent_only")
                )
                record["end_event_type"] = event_type
    return fluents


def _visible_to(agent_id, holder, visibility):
    return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id


def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
    """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
    visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
    cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
    as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
    round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
    two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
    currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
    renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
    interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
    that wrote the fact already authored."""
    results = []
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record.get("narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
            and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
            and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
        ):
            results.append(record)
        elif (
            record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
            and record.get("end_narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))
        ):
            results.append({**record, "narration": record["end_narration"]})
    return results


def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
    """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
    this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
    shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
    `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
    (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
    once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
    per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
    read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
    twice."""
    events = []
    for record in fluents:
        if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
            events.append(_memory_spec(

            events.append(_memory_spec(
                record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility", "agent_only"),
                record.get("end_event_type", "fact_ended"), record["end_narration"],
            ))
    return events

    agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder

        return {

            "constraints_line": f" {constraints_line}" if constraints_line else "",

1: # Recipe: new_rule (Level 3)
2: 
3: A deterministic constraint/consequence attaches to an existing action —
4: no new agent judgment. Read `rule-contract.md` in full before starting;
5: this recipe assumes it.
6: 
7: **First**: check `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types` catalog for an
8: existing type (on *any* action) close enough to reuse or generalize
9: parametrically — a real run wrote 10 separate files reimplementing the
10: same handful of shapes. Only proceed past this line if nothing fits.
11: 
12: | | |
13: |---|---|
14: | **Required** | `actions/rules/{action_name}/{name}.py` — a `Rule` subclass with a unique `type_name` (unique within that action's subdirectory), overriding only the hooks it needs. |
15: | **Required** | Add `{"type": "{name}", ...params}` to `state["config"]["rules"][action_name]` — **in the same round**. A file with no config entry runs never. |
16: | **Required** | Open the `rule_active` fluent for this activation (`set_fact`, `holder="community"`, `args={"action": action_name, "type": type_name}`). |
17: | **Conditional** | If `type_name` is genuinely new (not in `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types` catalog before): add `{name: {"description", "owner": "actions/rules/{action_name}/{name}.py"}}` there, once. |
18: | **Conditional** | `lifecycle` on the config entry if the norm implies a bounded duration — see `lifecycle_change.md`. |
19: | **Conditional** | If replacing the action's currently-active rule (the normal case for a new adopted norm): replace that action's list rather than append, unless the new norm's text genuinely leaves the old concern untouched. |
20: | **Conditional** | A short entry in `actions/rules/README.md` — only if this shape is genuinely reusable and worth documenting there for a future round, not for every rule. |
21: | **Required** | `tests/norm_checks/` test covering every new conditional branch, exercised through the real action handler (e.g. `actions.handlers.harvest.run(ctx)`) against a minimal fabricated state — not a unit test of the class in isolation. |
22: | **Forbidden** | Editing a protected action/handler. Touching `state/schedule.json`. Editing a *different* action's rule list unless the norm genuinely concerns that action too. A bare `self.params.get(key)` with no default — always supply one. |
23: | **Verify** | `python3 -m py_compile`. `pytest tests/norm_checks/ tests/regression/`. **Open `state/config.json` on disk and confirm the type actually appears there** — not your memory of having written it. Grep your new file for `.params.get(`/`self.params.get(` and confirm every match has a second argument. |
24: 
25: The activation step above is the single most common way a round is
26: written but never enforces anything — see `rule-contract.md`'s own
27: evidence (10 of 11 committed rounds on a real run).

1: # state/object_types/
2: 
3: One `{type_name}.json` file per institutional-object *type* (a pool, a
4: ledger, a permit, a tool) — the declarative `ObjectSpec` schema
5: `engine/institution/objects.py::ObjectRuntime` reads. Instances of a type
6: are *declared* in `state/objects.json` (`id`/`type`/an optional
7: `lifecycle` — never a field value), mirroring `actions/rules/{action_name}/`'s
8: own type/instance split (an `actions/rules/{action_name}/{type}.py` file
9: defines a shape; `state/config.json["rules"][action_name]` lists which
10: instances of it are active). This directory is only ever the catalog of
11: what *kinds* of object exist.
12: 
13: The actual mutable field values (a pool's current balance, a ledger's
14: entries) live in neither of those files — they're simulation-owned, in
15: `state["runtime"]["objects"][object_id]["fields"]`, seeded from this
16: file's own `fields` defaults the first time anything touches the object.
17: Keeping a declaration and its accumulating runtime values apart is
18: deliberate: exactly the same reason `state/config.json["rules"][action_name]`
19: entries never hold a rule's own running balance (that's
20: `runtime["rules"][key]`, via `ctx.rule_state(key)`) — a
21: norm-implementer-writable file must never also be where the running
22: simulation's own numbers live.
23: 
24: **Ships empty by design**, same principle and same reason as
25: `actions/rules/` (see that directory's own README): most norms that
26: introduce a communal pool or a shared ledger are fully expressible by
27: declaring a new type here — no seed content is included on purpose, so
28: the first norm that ever needs one is genuinely operationalized from
29: scratch, not just a pre-built shape with the numbers tuned.
30: 
31: ## Shape
32: 
33: ```json
34: {
35:   "type_name": "communal_pool",
36:   "description": "A shared reserve fishers deposit surplus into.",
37:   "ownership": "COMMUNAL",
38:   "fields": {"balance_kg": {"type": "number", "default": 0.0}},
39:   "operations": ["deposit", "withdraw", "read"],
40:   "permissions": {
41:     "WRITE": {"who": "ROLE:treasurer"},
42:     "READ": {"who": "ALL"}
43:   },
44:   "visibility": {
45:     "balance_kg": {"who": "ALL"}
46:   },
47:   "custom_handler": null,
48:   "introduced_round": 9
49: }
50: ```
51: 
52: `permissions` gates what an *operation* may do
53: (`ObjectRuntime.deposit()`/`.withdraw()`/`.set()`/`.append()`, checked
54: against `WRITE`/`APPEND` respectively — `who` is `"ALL"`, `"NONE"`, or
55: `"ROLE:<role_name>"`, resolved via `roles.roles.current_holder()`, never
56: cached). `visibility` gates what `ObjectRuntime.read()` returns to a given
57: viewer, per field — separate from permissions on purpose: an object can
58: be world-readable but role-write-gated, or the reverse.
59: 
60: `custom_handler`, when set, names a filename stem under
61: `objects/handlers/` (also ships empty — see that directory's own README)
62: implementing behavior beyond the five generic operations, dispatched via
63: `ObjectRuntime.custom(object_id, operation, ...)`. Reach for this only
64: when a generic deposit/withdraw/set/append/read genuinely can't express
65: what the norm needs — the same "declarative first, code only when truly
66: necessary" principle behind every other pluggable layer in this project.

import importlib
from dataclasses import dataclass

from engine.institution.lifecycle import is_active, tick
from engine.institution.registry import discover_subclasses


class Rule:
    """Base class for one entry under actions/rules/{action_name}/. Every
    hook is optional (all default to a no-op) — implement only the ones a
    given rule actually needs. `self.key`/`self.params` mirror the old
    Norm contract exactly (never persist anything on self between hooks;
    a fresh instance is built every round — use ctx.rule_state(self.key)
    for anything that must survive across rounds)."""

    type_name: str = None  # set by every subclass; unique within its own action's rule directory

    def __init__(self, key, params):
        self.key = key
        self.params = params

    # --- round-level: fires once per round, independent of any one action ---

    def before_round(self, state, round_number):
        """Once per round, before ANY action in this round's schedule has
        run. `state` is the full round-state dict (no single ActionContext
        exists yet at this point — nothing has been resolved to one
        action's participants)."""
        return None

    def after_round(self, state, round_number):
        """Once per round, after EVERY action in this round's schedule has
        already run."""
        return None

    # --- action-level: fires once per round for this rule's own action ---

    def before_action(self, ctx):
        """Once, before this action's own participants are processed this
        round. `ctx` is the action's ActionContext."""
        return None

    def after_action(self, ctx, round_record):
        """Once, after this action's round_record has been fully built —
        may mutate `round_record` and/or `ctx.state` directly (a stock
        override, a tally adjustment, a community-wide consequence). This
        is where a "the whole action's outcome" rule belongs, as opposed
        to a per-agent one."""
        return None

    # --- per-agent: only meaningful for an action whose handler calls
    # these explicitly inside its own per-agent loop (every handler in
    # this project does, including the generic Level-2 path) ---

    def is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id):
        """False skips this agent's LLM call entirely this round (a live
        ban). Called at most once per agent per round."""
        return True

    def describe(self, ctx, agent_id):
        """One already-in-world-phrased sentence describing whatever this
        rule currently has to say to this agent, or None. Every active
        rule's non-None output is joined into one constraints line."""
        return None

    def after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
        """Once per participating agent, right after their own
        record_entry dict has been built from their response — return a
        dict of fields to merge onto it (e.g. {"harvested_kg": 12.0,
        "note": "trimmed to the 15kg limit"}), or None for no change.

        seeing the previous rule's already-applied patch on
        `record_entry` — this is the ordering-dependent chain (a reserve
        rule seeing a cap rule's already-trimmed number) the old
        raw_kg/proposed_kg threading provided; a rule needing the
        pre-any-rule original value re-derives it from a field no rule
        touches (harvest's own "effort" field, say), the same technique
        `engine.llm_agents._harvest_shortfall_clause()` already uses."""
        return None

        applied its patch — `record_entry` here is the fully-settled
        final state, not the intermediate view after_agent() sees mid-chain.

        any one rule's own contribution to it (starting a ban countdown
        because the settled record turned out to be a violation, say).

        (ctx.rule_state(self.key), ctx.objects, ctx.events), never for
        further patching record_entry itself; use after_agent() for that."""

@dataclass
class RuleSet:
    """Every active Rule for one action this round, in
    state["config"]["rules"][action_name] order — built fresh per
    ActionContext (see engine.institution.context.ActionContext), never
    cached, so a norm-implementer's mid-run edit to a rule file takes
    effect immediately."""

    rules: list

    @classmethod
    def for_action(cls, config, action_name, round_number=None):
        """`round_number=None` (the default) validates every entry —
        type resolves, key is unique — and includes all of them,
        active or not; passing a real `round_number` additionally filters
        out anything whose own `lifecycle` has expired or not started."""
        rule_types = discover_rule_types(action_name)
        specs = config.get("rules", {}).get(action_name, [])
        rules = []
        seen_keys = set()
        for i, spec in enumerate(specs):
            rule_type = spec.get("type")
            rule_cls = rule_types.get(rule_type)
            if rule_cls is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"state/config.json rules[{action_name!r}][{i}]: unknown rule type "
                    f"{rule_type!r} — must be one of {sorted(rule_types)}"
                )
            key = spec.get("id", rule_type)
            if key in seen_keys:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"state/config.json rules[{action_name!r}][{i}]: duplicate rule key {key!r} "
                    f'— set an explicit "id" to disambiguate multiple rules of the same type'
                )
            seen_keys.add(key)
            if round_number is not None and not is_active(spec.get("lifecycle"), round_number):
                continue
            rules.append(rule_cls(key=key, params=spec))
        return cls(rules)

    def is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id):
        """AND across every active rule — one veto is enough to skip the
        LLM call. Every rule's is_eligible() still runs regardless (a ban
        countdown must always tick), only the combined boolean result
        short-circuits the call."""
        eligible = True
        for rule in self.rules:
            if not rule.is_eligible(ctx, agent_id):

28: def resolve_participants(spec, state):

30:     Default ("all_alive_fishers") is byte-identical to today's

32:     participation = spec.get("participation", {"policy": "all_alive_fishers"})
33:     policy = participation.get("policy", "all_alive_fishers")
34:     if policy == "all_alive_fishers":
35:         return alive_agent_ids(state["agents"], state["runtime"])
36:     if policy == "role_holders":
37:         role_name = participation["role"]

40:             record["holder"] for record in state["fluents"]
41:             if record["fluent"] == role_name
42:             and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
43:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)

50:     round-state dict: config/fluents/runtime/agents/round_number), the
51:     resolved participant list, `.agents` (AgentCaller), `.events`
52:     (EventEmitter — appends a point-in-time occurrence to

55:     state.get("object_types", {}) — loaded by engine.simulate.load_state()
56:     — plus state["objects"] (declarations) and state["runtime"]["objects"]
57:     (mutable field values, kept separate from the declaration exactly as
58:     runtime["rules"][key] is kept separate from a rule's own config
59:     entry)), and `.rules` (a RuleSet — every Rule configured for THIS
60:     action, in state["config"]["rules"][spec["name"]] order; see
61:     engine.institution.rules). Every action gets the identical `.rules`
62:     access — nothing about this class treats any one action specially,
63:     which is the whole point: a rule attaches the same way to any action,
64:     not just harvest."""

1: # ActionRuntime: the one thing engine/simulate.py calls per action per
2: # round, replacing the old `action_module.ACTION.run(state)`. Resolves an
3: # ActionSpec's execution.handler to either a builtin (Level 2, zero code)
4: # or a discovered actions/handlers/{name}.py function (Level 3/4, or one of
5: # the 5 protected actions ported 1:1), calls it, and finishes the
6: # round-record bookkeeping every handler used to have to do for itself.
7: 
8: import importlib
9: 
10: from engine.institution import builtin_handlers
11: from engine.institution.context import ActionContext
12: 
13: 
14: def resolve_handler(handler_name):
15:     """A builtin (an attribute of engine.institution.builtin_handlers)
16:     takes precedence by name; otherwise `handler_name` is a filename stem
17:     under actions/handlers/. Raises immediately, with a clear message, if
18:     neither resolves — the same fail-fast posture
19:     engine.institution.rules.RuleSet.for_action() already has for an
20:     unknown rule type."""
21:     builtin = getattr(builtin_handlers, handler_name, None)
22:     if callable(builtin):
23:         return builtin
24:     try:
25:         module = importlib.import_module(f"actions.handlers.{handler_name}")
26:     except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
27:         raise ValueError(
28:             f"execution.handler {handler_name!r} is neither a builtin "
29:             f"(engine.institution.builtin_handlers) nor actions/handlers/{handler_name}.py"

1: # Institutional architecture — conceptual model
2: 
3: Read this once per round, before classifying requirements. The other
4: contract files in this directory go deeper on one piece each; this one is
5: the map of how the pieces fit together.
6: 
7: ## The atomic unit: an action
8: 
9: An **action** is the atomic unit of agent decision-making — one
10: `call_fisher_agent()` call per action, per round (`harvest`, `propose`,
11: `critique`, `vote`, `discuss` today). "Decision" is broad: reporting,
12: inspecting, voting on a sanction, choosing to close something all count,
13: exactly as much as an effort/cap choice does.
14: 
15: Every requirement in an accepted norm routes to exactly one of four
16: levels, ordered by cost. Route by what the requirement actually **is**,
17: never by which level is cheapest to build:
18: 
19: | Level | Shape | Cost |
20: |---|---|---|
21: | **1** | A config value on an already-active rule type, or a `lifecycle` added to an existing rule/action/object entry. | No new file. |
22: | **2** | A new declarative institutional object, or a new action built entirely from the generic handler (`execution.handler: "generic_agent_decision"` — ask one question, record the answer). | One spec/type file, zero Python. |
23: | **3** | A new `actions/rules/{action}/{name}.py` type, or a small custom `actions/handlers/{name}.py` / `objects/handlers/{type}.py`. | Real logic, bounded by a fixed hook contract. |
24: | **4** | A genuinely new institutional decision no existing action/handler shape hosts. | Full new-action recipe, its own handler. |
25: 
26: A Level-4 action is one `run(ctx)` function, not a class hierarchy — read
27: `action-contract.md` before pricing anything as "too much new
28: infrastructure."
29: 
30: ## Deterministic constraint vs. genuine agent judgment
31: 
32: A **rule** (`actions/rules/{action}/*.py`) is arithmetic over values that
33: already exist — a cap, a fee, a reserve deposit, a ban countdown. It has
34: no judgment. A verb where an actor weighs, judges, inspects, decides,
35: reviews-and-rules, verifies, contests, appeals, testifies, or exercises
36: discretion using information not already reduced to a number/boolean is
37: **action-shaped**, not rule-shaped, regardless of how much simpler a rule
38: file would be to write. Two failure directions are equally real: routing
39: a genuine judgment call into a rule file means the "decision" is never
40: actually made by anyone (a real round did this with a rotating "verifier"
41: who was supposed to weigh evidence and impose bans — nobody was ever
42: banned, because the decision was silently reduced to a comparison);
43: routing genuine arithmetic into a new action wastes a Level-4 budget for
44: no reason. Cost is never itself a legitimate reason to pick one over the
45: other.
46: 
47: A second, easy-to-miss action-shaped trigger: an actor **producing** a
48: value through their own perception/sampling/judgment (estimates, samples,
49: surveys, reports, observes) — action-shaped even when the simulation
50: already knows the "true" number internally. Silently substituting the
51: known value and labeling it "their estimate" deletes the institution the
52: norm described, it doesn't approximate it (a real round did exactly this
53: with a "watcher" whose stock estimate was just the real physics value
54: relabeled — no fisher was ever actually asked, for three rounds).
55: 
56: ## Inventory vs. decision vs. rule
57: 
58: A third, orthogonal question: is this a decision at all, or is it
59: **inventory**? A communal pool, a ledger, a permit's remaining allowance
60: is state something else (a rule, an action) reads and writes — never a
61: decision anyone makes, never a new action just because the norm's text
62: introduces a new noun. See `object-contract.md`.
63: 
64: ## Roles: structure vs. current holder
65: 
66: `state/institution.json`'s `roles` catalog and an action's own
67: `actor_role` describe **structure** — does this role exist, does it
68: rotate, does this action require it. They never say who holds it right
69: now. That's a live lookup, `roles.roles.current_holder(fluents,
70: role_name, round_number)`, answered fresh every time from
71: `state/fluents.json` — never cached in `state/institution.json`, because
72: that file only changes when the institution's *shape* changes, not every
73: round a rotation fires. See `role-contract.md`.
74: 
75: ## Current-state files vs. history
76: 
77: `state/config.json` (rules) and `state/objects.json` (object instances)
78: show **current** state only. History lives elsewhere and is written
79: automatically, not by you: `state/institution_history.jsonl` (structural
80: changes, orchestrator-appended), and a `rule_active` fluent (when a rule
81: type was active, for which action, for how long — you open/close this
82: one yourself, see `rule-contract.md`).
83: 
84: ## Interval facts vs. point-in-time occurrences
85: 
86: `state/fluents.json` holds **interval** facts — a genuine start and
87: possibly an end (roles, bans, `rule_active`). `state/events.json` holds
88: **point-in-time** occurrences — an object mutation, a one-off
89: announcement, nothing with a duration. Both are populated by simulation
90: code at run time (`ctx.events.emit(...)`, `ObjectRuntime`'s own
91: `narration` kwarg, `roles.roles.set_fact()`/`end_fact()`) — you almost
92: never hand-edit either file's content directly, only their *schema*
93: (`state/fluents_schema.md` for new fluent names).
94: 
95: ## Compiled artifacts — never hand-edited
96: 
97: `state/schedule.json` is compiled every round from `state/institution.json`'s
98: action catalog plus each `state/actions/{name}.json`'s own
99: `scheduling.after`/`before`/`gate`. Need a new action to run between two
100: existing ones? That's an `after`/`before` value in the new action's own
101: spec — never a `state/schedule.json` edit (denied outright by
102: permission, and solving the wrong problem if you're tempted).
103: 
104: ## Protected paths — additive only, permanently
105: 
106: `state/actions/{harvest,propose,critique,vote,discuss}.json` and their
107: `actions/handlers/*.py` pairs are permanently off-limits — and so is
108: every action any earlier round has ever added. "Additive only" doesn't
109: loosen after the first new action exists; a second round needing
110: something close to an earlier new action still gets its own new action,
111: never an edit to the first one. Enforced by a hard, dynamic orchestrator
112: check (`_actions_protected_as_of_head()` in `engine/simulate.py`, which
113: reads `state/institution.json` as of HEAD and protects everything it
114: lists, not just the original five) — independent of whatever the
115: permission YAML does or doesn't block.
116: 
117: ## Reuse before creating
118: 
119: Before writing any new rule type, action, or object type, check
120: `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types`/`object_types` catalogs (fast,
121: already-summarized, and each entry's `owner` path tells you which action
122: it belongs to) — a real run accumulated 10 separate rule files
123: reimplementing the same handful of cap/reserve shapes from scratch,
124: never once reusing an earlier one.

(End of file - total 124 lines)

1: # Recipe: new_rule (Level 3)
2: 
3: A deterministic constraint/consequence attaches to an existing action —
4: no new agent judgment. Read `rule-contract.md` in full before starting;
5: this recipe assumes it.
6: 
7: **First**: check `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types` catalog for an
8: existing type (on *any* action) close enough to reuse or generalize
9: parametrically — a real run wrote 10 separate files reimplementing the
10: same handful of shapes. Only proceed past this line if nothing fits.
11: 
12: | | |
13: |---|---|
14: | **Required** | `actions/rules/{action_name}/{name}.py` — a `Rule` subclass with a unique `type_name` (unique within that action's subdirectory), overriding only the hooks it needs. |
15: | **Required** | Add `{"type": "{name}", ...params}` to `state["config"]["rules"][action_name]` — **in the same round**. A file with no config entry runs never. |
16: | **Required** | Open the `rule_active` fluent for this activation (`set_fact`, `holder="community"`, `args={"action": action_name, "type": type_name}`). |
17: | **Conditional** | If `type_name` is genuinely new (not in `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types` catalog before): add `{name: {"description", "owner": "actions/rules/{action_name}/{name}.py"}}` there, once. |
18: | **Conditional** | `lifecycle` on the config entry if the norm implies a bounded duration — see `lifecycle_change.md`. |
19: | **Conditional** | If replacing the action's currently-active rule (the normal case for a new adopted norm): replace that action's list rather than append, unless the new norm's text genuinely leaves the old concern untouched. |
20: | **Conditional** | A short entry in `actions/rules/README.md` — only if this shape is genuinely reusable and worth documenting there for a future round, not for every rule. |
21: | **Required** | `tests/norm_checks/` test covering every new conditional branch, exercised through the real action handler (e.g. `actions.handlers.harvest.run(ctx)`) against a minimal fabricated state — not a unit test of the class in isolation. |
22: | **Forbidden** | Editing a protected action/handler. Touching `state/schedule.json`. Editing a *different* action's rule list unless the norm genuinely concerns that action too. A bare `self.params.get(key)` with no default — always supply one. |
23: | **Verify** | `python3 -m py_compile`. `pytest tests/norm_checks/ tests/regression/`. **Open `state/config.json` on disk and confirm the type actually appears there** — not your memory of having written it. Grep your new file for `.params.get(`/`self.params.get(` and confirm every match has a second argument. |
24: 
25: The activation step above is the single most common way a round is
26: written but never enforces anything — see `rule-contract.md`'s own
27: evidence (10 of 11 committed rounds on a real run).

from roles.roles import set_fact, end_fact
from engine.institution.agent_loop import per_agent_decision
from engine.physics import (
    catch_from_effort,
    apply_regrowth,
    apply_consumption,
    is_dead,
    available_stock,
    CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
)


def run(ctx):
    state = ctx.state
    runtime = state["runtime"]
    fluents = state["fluents"]
    round_number = ctx.round_number

    runtime.setdefault("payoff", {})
    runtime.setdefault("dead_agents", [])
    stock_before = available_stock(runtime)

    def build_fields(agent_id):
        constraints_line = ctx.rules.describe_constraints(ctx, agent_id)
        return {
            "stock_kg": stock_before,
            "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
            "constraints_line": f" {constraints_line}" if constraints_line else "",
            "stock_trend": _stock_trend(runtime, state["config"], round_number),
        }

    def build_record(agent_id, response):
        effort = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(response["effort"])))
        raw_kg = catch_from_effort(effort, stock_before)
        return {"effort": effort, "harvested_kg": raw_kg, "reasoning": response.get("reasoning", ""), "note": None}

    def after_settle(agent_id, record_entry):
        new_payoff = apply_consumption(runtime["payoff"].get(agent_id, 0.0), record_entry["harvested_kg"])
        runtime["payoff"][agent_id] = new_payoff
        if is_dead(new_payoff):
            runtime["dead_agents"].append(agent_id)
            name = state["agents"][agent_id]["name"]
            set_fact(
                fluents, "dead", [agent_id], agent_id, round_number,
                narration=f"{name} has died — they hadn't been catching enough fish to survive.",
                visibility="public",
            )
            end_fact(fluents, "fisher", [agent_id], round_number)

    def ineligible_record(agent_id):
        return {
            "effort": None, "harvested_kg": 0.0, "reasoning": "",
            "note": ctx.rules.ineligibility_note(ctx, agent_id), "participated": False,
        }

    agent_records = per_agent_decision(
        ctx, build_fields, build_record, ineligible_record=ineligible_record, after_settle=after_settle,
    )

    stock_after_harvest = stock_before - sum(r["harvested_kg"] for r in agent_records.values())
    stock_after_regrowth = apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest)
    runtime["stock_kg"] = stock_after_regrowth

    # A rule that needs to override the round's own final stock number
    # (a "replenish the lake" trigger, say) does so from its own
    # after_action(ctx, round_record) hook — called generically by
    # ActionRuntime right after this function returns — by writing
    # ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"] and round_record["stock_kg_after_regrowth"]
    # directly; no special override method is needed here for that.
    return {
        "agents": agent_records,
        "stock_kg_before": stock_before,
        "stock_kg_after_harvest": stock_after_harvest,
        "stock_kg_after_regrowth": stock_after_regrowth,
    }

from engine.physics import alive_agent_ids
from engine.institution.events import EventEmitter
from engine.institution.objects import ObjectRuntime
from engine.institution.rules import RuleSet


class AgentCaller:
    """`ctx.agents` — calls the unmodified engine.llm_agents.call_fisher_agent()
    for this action, so a handler never needs to import or know about
    persona/prompt rendering itself."""

    def __init__(self, action_name, round_number):
        self.action_name = action_name
        self.round_number = round_number

    def call(self, agent_id, **fields):
        from engine.llm_agents import call_fisher_agent
        return call_fisher_agent(agent_id, self.round_number, self.action_name, **fields)


def resolve_participants(spec, state):
    """The participants for this round, per ActionSpec["participation"].
    Default ("all_alive_fishers") is byte-identical to today's
    alive_agent_ids() — every existing action's real behavior."""
    participation = spec.get("participation", {"policy": "all_alive_fishers"})
    policy = participation.get("policy", "all_alive_fishers")
    if policy == "all_alive_fishers":
        return alive_agent_ids(state["agents"], state["runtime"])
    if policy == "role_holders":
        role_name = participation["role"]
        round_number = state["round_number"]
        return [
            record["holder"] for record in state["fluents"]
            if record["fluent"] == role_name
            and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
            and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
        ]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown participation policy {policy!r}")


class ActionContext:
    """`ctx` — spec (this action's own ActionSpec dict), state (the full
    round-state dict: config/fluents/runtime/agents/round_number), the
    resolved participant list, `.agents` (AgentCaller), `.events`
    (EventEmitter — appends a point-in-time occurrence to
    state["events"], never a fact with a duration; see
    engine.institution.events), `.objects` (ObjectRuntime, built from
    state.get("object_types", {}) — loaded by engine.simulate.load_state()
    — plus state["objects"] (declarations) and state["runtime"]["objects"]
    (mutable field values, kept separate from the declaration exactly as
    runtime["rules"][key] is kept separate from a rule's own config
    entry)), and `.rules` (a RuleSet — every Rule configured for THIS
    action, in state["config"]["rules"][spec["name"]] order; see
    engine.institution.rules). Every action gets the identical `.rules`
    access — nothing about this class treats any one action specially,
    which is the whole point: a rule attaches the same way to any action,
    not just harvest."""

    def __init__(self, spec, state, round_number, participants):
        self.spec = spec
        self.state = state
        self.round_number = round_number
        self.participants = participants
        self.agents = AgentCaller(spec["name"], round_number)
        self.events = EventEmitter(
            state.setdefault("events", []), state["fluents"], round_number, participants=participants,
        )
        self.objects = ObjectRuntime(
            state.get("object_types", {}), state.setdefault("objects", []),
            state["runtime"].setdefault("objects", {}),
            state["fluents"], round_number, self.events,
        )
        self.rules = RuleSet.for_action(state["config"], spec["name"], round_number)
        self._scratch = {}

    def rule_state(self, key):
        """Cross-round-persistent state for the rule with this key — a
        reserve balance, a ban countdown. Backed by runtime["rules"][key],
        saved to state/runtime.json like everything else the simulation
        writes — never pre-seeded by the norm-implementer directly."""
        return self.state["runtime"].setdefault("rules", {}).setdefault(key, {})

    def round_scratch(self, key):
        """This-round-only state for the rule with this key (a running
        per-action tally, say) — lives only on this ActionContext
        instance, never persisted. A fresh ActionContext is built for
        every action call, so this always starts empty; use rule_state()
        for anything that must survive to a later round."""
        return self._scratch.setdefault(key, {})

1: # Rule: the generic per-action extension point that replaces the old,
2: # harvest-only norms/*.py + NormEngine mechanism. A Rule attaches to
3: # exactly one action (state/config.json["rules"][action_name]) and can
4: # hook every stage of that action's execution — round-wide, whole-action,
5: # and per-agent — plus the two round-boundary hooks that run once
6: # regardless of which actions execute this round. This directly answers
7: # the actual structural problem the old design had: only harvest ever
8: # built a NormEngine, so only harvest could host a rule at all. Every
9: # action now has the identical mechanism available; whether a given round
10: # actually needs one is a real question, not a foregone one.
11: #
12: # Files live under actions/rules/{action_name}/ — one subpackage per
13: # action, auto-discovered by type_name the same way the old norms/
14: # directory was (engine.institution.registry.discover_subclasses), so
15: # adding a new rule is still "add a file," never a registry edit. Ships
16: # empty for every action, same "no seed content" principle norms/ always
17: # had — a pre-built shape would let a round tune parameters on an
18: # already-correct implementation instead of writing one from scratch.
19: 
20: import importlib
21: from dataclasses import dataclass
22: 
23: from engine.institution.lifecycle import is_active, tick
24: from engine.institution.registry import discover_subclasses
25: 
26: 
27: class Rule:
28:     """Base class for one entry under actions/rules/{action_name}/. Every
29:     hook is optional (all default to a no-op) — implement only the ones a
30:     given rule actually needs. `self.key`/`self.params` mirror the old
31:     Norm contract exactly (never persist anything on self between hooks;
32:     a fresh instance is built every round — use ctx.rule_state(self.key)
33:     for anything that must survive across rounds)."""
34: 
35:     type_name: str = None  # set by every subclass; unique within its own action's rule directory
36: 
37:     def __init__(self, key, params):
38:         self.key = key
39:         self.params = params
40: 
41:     # --- round-level: fires once per round, independent of any one action ---
42: 
43:     def before_round(self, state, round_number):

import importlib
from dataclasses import dataclass

from engine.institution.lifecycle import is_active, tick
from engine.institution.registry import discover_subclasses


class Rule:
    """Base class for one entry under actions/rules/{action_name}/. Every
    hook is optional (all default to a no-op) — implement only the ones a
    given rule actually needs. `self.key`/`self.params` mirror the old
    Norm contract exactly (never persist anything on self between hooks;
    a fresh instance is built every round — use ctx.rule_state(self.key)
    for anything that must survive across rounds)."""

    type_name: str = None  # set by every subclass; unique within its own action's rule directory

    def __init__(self, key, params):
        self.key = key
        self.params = params

    # --- round-level: fires once per round, independent of any one action ---

    def before_round(self, state, round_number):
        """Once per round, before ANY action in this round's schedule has
        run. `state` is the full round-state dict (no single ActionContext
        exists yet at this point — nothing has been resolved to one
        action's participants)."""
        return None

    def after_round(self, state, round_number):
        """Once per round, after EVERY action in this round's schedule has
        already run."""
        return None

    # --- action-level: fires once per round for this rule's own action ---

    def before_action(self, ctx):
        """Once, before this action's own participants are processed this
        round. `ctx` is the action's ActionContext."""
        return None

    def after_action(self, ctx, round_record):
        """Once, after this action's round_record has been fully built —
        may mutate `round_record` and/or `ctx.state` directly (a stock
        override, a tally adjustment, a community-wide consequence). This
        is where a "the whole action's outcome" rule belongs, as opposed
        to a per-agent one."""
        return None

    # --- per-agent: only meaningful for an action whose handler calls
    # these explicitly inside its own per-agent loop (every handler in
    # this project does, including the generic Level-2 path) ---

    def is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id):
        """False skips this agent's LLM call entirely this round (a live
        ban). Called at most once per agent per round."""
        return True

    def describe(self, ctx, agent_id):
        """One already-in-world-phrased sentence describing whatever this
        rule currently has to say to this agent, or None. Every active
        rule's non-None output is joined into one constraints line."""
        return None

    def after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
        """Once per participating agent, right after their own
        record_entry dict has been built from their response — return a
        dict of fields to merge onto it (e.g. {"harvested_kg": 12.0,
        "note": "trimmed to the 15kg limit"}), or None for no change.

        seeing the previous rule's already-applied patch on

        touches (harvest's own "effort" field, say), the same technique
        `engine.llm_agents._harvest_shortfall_clause()` already uses."""
        return None

        applied its patch — `record_entry` here is the fully-settled
        final state, not the intermediate view after_agent() sees mid-chain.

        any one rule's own contribution to it (starting a ban countdown
        because the settled record turned out to be a violation, say).
        Return value is ignored — this hook is for side effects
        (ctx.rule_state(self.key), ctx.objects, ctx.events), never for
        further patching record_entry itself; use after_agent() for that."""
        return None


@dataclass
class RuleSet:
    """Every active Rule for one action this round, in
    state["config"]["rules"][action_name] order — built fresh per
    ActionContext (see engine.institution.context.ActionContext), never
    cached, so a norm-implementer's mid-run edit to a rule file takes
    effect immediately."""

    rules: list

    @classmethod
    def for_action(cls, config, action_name, round_number=None):
        """`round_number=None` (the default) validates every entry —
        type resolves, key is unique — and includes all of them,
        active or not; passing a real `round_number` additionally filters
        out anything whose own `lifecycle` has expired or not started."""
        rule_types = discover_rule_types(action_name)
        specs = config.get("rules", {}).get(action_name, [])
        rules = []
        seen_keys = set()
        for i, spec in enumerate(specs):
            rule_type = spec.get("type")
            rule_cls = rule_types.get(rule_type)
            if rule_cls is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"state/config.json rules[{action_name!r}][{i}]: unknown rule type "
                    f"{rule_type!r} — must be one of {sorted(rule_types)}"
                )
            key = spec.get("id", rule_type)
            if key in seen_keys:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"state/config.json rules[{action_name!r}][{i}]: duplicate rule key {key!r} "
                    f'— set an explicit "id" to disambiguate multiple rules of the same type'
                )
            seen_keys.add(key)
            if round_number is not None and not is_active(spec.get("lifecycle"), round_number):
                continue
            rules.append(rule_cls(key=key, params=spec))
        return cls(rules)

    def is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id):
        """AND across every active rule — one veto is enough to skip the
        LLM call. Every rule's is_eligible() still runs regardless (a ban
        countdown must always tick), only the combined boolean result
        short-circuits the call."""
        eligible = True
        for rule in self.rules:
            if not rule.is_eligible(ctx, agent_id):
                eligible = False
        return eligible

    def describe_constraints(self, ctx, agent_id):
        lines = (rule.describe(ctx, agent_id) for rule in self.rules)
        return " ".join(line for line in lines if line)

    def ineligibility_note(self, ctx, agent_id):
        return self.describe_constraints(ctx, agent_id) or (
            "Something about the community's current rules held you back this round."
        )

    def apply_after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
        """Runs every rule's after_agent() in order, merging each
        returned patch onto record_entry in place — a "note" value
        concatenates onto any existing one (so two contributing rules
        both get heard) rather than overwriting it; every other field is
        a plain overwrite. Returns record_entry for convenience."""
        for rule in self.rules:
            patch = rule.after_agent(ctx, agent_id, record_entry)
            if not patch:
                continue
            for field_name, value in patch.items():
                if field_name == "note" and record_entry.get("note") and value:
                    record_entry["note"] = f"{record_entry['note']} {value}".strip()
                else:
                    record_entry[field_name] = value
        return record_entry

    def settle_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
        """Call once, right after apply_after_agent() — runs every rule's
        on_agent_settled() with the now-fully-patched record_entry.
        Kept as its own explicit call (not folded into apply_after_agent()
        itself) so a handler can inspect/log the settled record between
        the two if it wants to, and so it's obvious at the call site that
        every rule's own patch is already final by the time settlement
        hooks run."""
        for rule in self.rules:
            rule.on_agent_settled(ctx, agent_id, record_entry)

    def before_action(self, ctx):
        for rule in self.rules:
            rule.before_action(ctx)

    def after_action(self, ctx, round_record):
        for rule in self.rules:
            rule.after_action(ctx, round_record)


def discover_rule_types(action_name):
    """Every Rule subclass under actions/rules/{action_name}/, keyed by
    type_name — {} if that action has no rules directory at all yet (a
    brand-new action nobody has attached a rule to), never an error."""
    try:
        package = importlib.import_module(f"actions.rules.{action_name}")
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        return {}
    return discover_subclasses(package, Rule, "type_name")


def all_configured_rules(config, round_number=None):
    """Every Rule instance across every action in
    state["config"]["rules"], flattened — what engine/simulate.py's
    run_cycle() calls before_round()/after_round() on, since those two
    hooks fire once per round regardless of which action a rule is
    otherwise attached to."""
    rules = []
    for action_name in config.get("rules", {}):
        rules.extend(RuleSet.for_action(config, action_name, round_number).rules)
    return rules

import engine.institution.rules as rules_module
import engine.llm_agents as llm_agents_module
import actions.handlers.harvest as harvest_handler
from engine.institution.context import ActionContext
from engine.institution.rules import Rule
from engine.physics import apply_consumption, apply_regrowth, catch_from_effort

# The deterministic proof that harvest's own physics, plus the generic
# per-agent rule hooks (is_eligible/after_agent) every action now exposes,
# produce the exact numbers they always have — with no rule configured at
# all, and with one actually attached.

EFFORTS = {"agent_0": 0.5, "agent_1": 0.2}
SPEC = {"name": "harvest"}


def _fake_call_fisher_agent(agent_id, round_number, action_name, **fields):
    return {"effort": EFFORTS[agent_id], "reasoning": "test"}


def _state(rules_config=None):
    return {
        "config": {"rules": {"harvest": rules_config or []}},
        "fluents": [],
        "runtime": {"stock_kg": 300.0, "rounds": []},
        "agents": {
            "agent_0": {"name": "Kai", "personality_traits": ""},
            "agent_1": {"name": "Mara", "personality_traits": ""},
        },
        "round_number": 1,
    }


def _run(state):
    ctx = ActionContext.build(SPEC, state, state["round_number"])
    return harvest_handler.run(ctx)


def test_baseline_empty_rules_matches_hand_computed_physics(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm_agents_module, "call_fisher_agent", _fake_call_fisher_agent)
    state = _state()

    record = _run(state)

    raw_0 = catch_from_effort(0.5, 300.0)
    raw_1 = catch_from_effort(0.2, 300.0)
    assert record["agents"]["agent_0"]["harvested_kg"] == pytest.approx(raw_0)
    assert record["agents"]["agent_1"]["harvested_kg"] == pytest.approx(raw_1)
    assert record["agents"]["agent_0"]["note"] is None
    assert record["agents"]["agent_1"]["note"] is None
    assert record["agents"]["agent_0"]["participated"] is True

    stock_after_harvest = 300.0 - (raw_0 + raw_1)
    assert record["stock_kg_after_harvest"] == pytest.approx(stock_after_harvest)
    assert record["stock_kg_after_regrowth"] == pytest.approx(apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest))

    expected_payoff_0 = apply_consumption(0.0, raw_0)
    expected_payoff_1 = apply_consumption(0.0, raw_1)
    assert state["runtime"]["payoff"]["agent_0"] == pytest.approx(expected_payoff_0)
    assert state["runtime"]["payoff"]["agent_1"] == pytest.approx(expected_payoff_1)
    assert state["runtime"]["dead_agents"] == []


def test_baseline_no_rules_state_key_created_when_rules_empty(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm_agents_module, "call_fisher_agent", _fake_call_fisher_agent)
    state = _state()
    _run(state)
    assert "rules" not in state["runtime"]


class _FakeCap(Rule):
    type_name = "_fake_cap_for_handler_test"

    def after_agent(self, ctx, agent_id, record_entry):
        limit = self.params.get("limit_kg", 999999)
        if record_entry["harvested_kg"] > limit:
            return {"harvested_kg": limit, "note": f"trimmed to the {limit}kg limit"}
        return None


class _FakeBan(Rule):
    type_name = "_fake_ban_for_handler_test"

    def is_eligible(self, ctx, agent_id):
        return not ctx.rule_state(self.key).get(agent_id, False)


def _fake_discover(rule_types_by_action):
    return lambda action_name: rule_types_by_action.get(action_name, {})


def test_a_configured_rule_actually_constrains_the_result(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm_agents_module, "call_fisher_agent", _fake_call_fisher_agent)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        rules_module, "discover_rule_types",
        _fake_discover({"harvest": {"_fake_cap_for_handler_test": _FakeCap}}),
    )
    state = _state(rules_config=[{"type": "_fake_cap_for_handler_test", "limit_kg": 1.0}])

    record = _run(state)

    assert record["agents"]["agent_0"]["harvested_kg"] == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert record["agents"]["agent_0"]["note"] is not None
    assert "1.0kg limit" in record["agents"]["agent_0"]["note"]

    call_log = []

HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY = 0.05  # catchability coefficient q in catch_from_effort()
GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()
CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG = 300  # lake's ceiling, also its starting stock
CONSUMPTION_KG = 1.0  # fixed per-round cost every fisher owes just to get by


def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
    is their catchability coefficient q."""
    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY


def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)


def apply_consumption(payoff, harvested_kg):
    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG

    permanent once true; nothing in this project ever resurrects an agent."""
    return payoff < 0

    rewrite the way a hand-rolled check per action could be."""
    dead = set(runtime.get("dead_agents", []))
    return [agent_id for agent_id in agents if agent_id not in dead]

def set_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
):
    """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
    exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
    the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
    non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
    tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
    "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.

    `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
    (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
    `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
    record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
    how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
    holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
    migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
    `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
    agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
    `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
    monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
    public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
    agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.

    Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
    layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
    picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
    entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
    fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
    `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
